messages.subject: Re: Correct way of determining the type of REXP
messages.subject_clean: Correct way of determining the type of REXP
messages.body_plain:
On Aug 24, 2008, at 12:14 PM, victualius at gmx.de wrote:

> as the getType() function in REXP.java is deprecated I guess I need  
> to determine the type using the is...() functions. Is there any  
> 'good' way in doing so, e.g. first checking for matrix/vector and  
> then checking for string/numeric?
>

I'm not quite sure what you are trying to do. The isXX() methods are  
essentially mappings from the corresponding is.xxx functions in R. The  
getType() approach is bad design, because it reflects the internal  
implementation and not the functionality. However, the implementation  
may change rendering code that relies on getType useless (as it did in  
0.5).


> Another question: The plotDemo example uses a JPEG transmitted as  
> RAW stream. Is there any way of telling there is a picture coming  
> through the connection? I have a small applet using Rserve to  
> evaluate user input and want to avoid parsing *any* binary data as a  
> picture.
>

Again, I'm not sure I know what you mean. Since you are in control of  
the evaluated code, you know how to interpret it. Somehow I don't see  
how you could end up receiving data you don't know about...


> I might maybe check the first bytes of the RAW stream but maybe  
> there is something better.
>

That depends solely on your application ...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Best way to transfer files generated in Rserve server to Java client.
messages.subject_clean: Best way to transfer files generated in Rserve server to Java client.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon, and others, 

As you probably remember, we (NKI, HMS and IMCB) are using Rserve to run Rpackages from a Java web application called Screensaver. One of the users will run Rserver on a seperate machine as Tomcat. The Rpackage in question , cellHTS2, will generate a report on the filesystem with different html pages and images. However, these files have to be stored in a subdirectory of the Tomcat installation directory, that is on the other machine. Can you advise us the best way to transfer the data within the same connection from the Rserve server to the Java client, in  this case the Tomcat machine?  A solution suggested by IMCB is to use the  Rserve class RFileInputStream which transfers files from Rserve server to the client. However it seems to transfer one file at a time. Zipping would be probably
  an answer, although it is not clear to us how you can do that from Rserve and/or R.

Thanks for your reply in advance!

Cor

messages.subject: problem occured dyna.load(rJava.dll)
messages.body_plain:
Hello all of you

First of all I want to thank you for creating rJava / JRI. I am currently
struggling to find a suitable environment for my diploma thesis in Data
Mining and now looking forward to combine R and RapidMiner(Yale)
for a mixture of rapid prototyping and reliable functions.

Starting with rJava today, I stumbled upon something weird. Installing the
package works, then
I tried to load it, which results in the following error:

"unable to load shared library" '<correct-path>/rJava.dll'


Ok. Setting up the path, looking for dyna.load(...) in the manual...so: I
fired up my RGUI and
set the working directory to the .../rJava/libs - directory and invoked
dyna.load() directly.
Results:
WinRegistry.dll has been loaded without problems,
rJava.dll-error occured again (same message)

Unable to find the error, I tried the same at my home computer and it
worked,for both libraries.

Here is my suspicion:
At my first workstation I was not logged in as an administrator/superuser.
Thankfully I have full rights on the
directory where R is installed, but I am allowed to read only on the
JAVA_HOME directory.

My system stats (both computers):
Windows XP, Service Pack 2

Browsing through the source of rJava I was not able to find the point
where the rJava.dll is created. So:
What is so special in the rJava.dll  that may have caused this error ?
Which rights (if my suspicion is correct)
have to be granted so that this error cannot occur ? Any ideas, suggestions ?

Thanks in advance

cheers,

Steffen

PS: I was thinking to post this question to the general R mailing list,
but since dyna.load() worked for WinRegistry.dll,
I decided to post it here (first).

> I have the same problem with the rJava namespace load failed. I'm also

> permissions because I can upload it if start R as root, but I can not

Stephan Wahlbrink (of StatET fame) discovered that
the problem occurs when one defines a JAVA_HOME
before calling R. After commenting the following
line from my .bashrc

export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-6-sun

and restarting a shell, I could launch R and
load the rJava package without any problem
(as a regular, non-root user).

The reason why this interferes with the process
of loading the rJava package is yet not very
clear to me, but I hope this trick solves your
problem as well.

Kind regards,
Tobias

messages.body_plain:
Hi list,

it's a common question I think, but I couldn't find solution in the  
archives...

In my project there is a linux machine running Rserve. My Java code,  
using Rserve, is running fine on this machine. Now I try to use  
Rserve via a remote connection from a windows machine.

At first I had a look at the settings using R CMD Rserve -RS-- 
settings and got:

config file: /etc/Rserv.conf
working root: /tmp/Rserc
port: 6311
local socket: [none, TCP/IP used]
authorization required: no
plain text password: not allowed
password file: [none]
allow I/O: yes
max.input buffer size: 262144 kB

I tried to locate the config file, but couldn't find it in $RHOME/ 
etc/. Therefore I created one with "remote enable" as the only entry.  
Unfortunately the settings did not change.
Then I tried to explicitly specify the config file in $RHOME/etc/  
using --RS-conf and also a new file in another directory. Nothing  
changed.

Trying to establish a remote connection I get a RserveException:  
Handshake failed... .

What did I wrong?

Christian

Christian,

On Sep 24, 2008, at 4:14 , System.out.println at web.de wrote:

> Hi list,
>
> it's a common question I think, but I couldn't find solution in the  
> archives...
>
> In my project there is a linux machine running Rserve. My Java code,  
> using Rserve, is running fine on this machine. Now I try to use  
> Rserve via a remote connection from a windows machine.
>
> At first I had a look at the settings using R CMD Rserve -RS-- 
> settings and got:
>
> config file: /etc/Rserv.conf
> working root: /tmp/Rserc
> port: 6311
> local socket: [none, TCP/IP used]
> authorization required: no
> plain text password: not allowed
> password file: [none]
> allow I/O: yes
> max.input buffer size: 262144 kB
>
> I tried to locate the config file, but couldn't find it in $RHOME/ 
> etc/.

There is none unless you create one.


> Therefore I created one with "remote enable" as the only entry.
> Unfortunately the settings did not change.

The above doesn't show the "remote" setting, so you wouldn't see any  
difference unless you changed one of the reported settings.


> Then I tried to explicitly specify the config file in $RHOME/etc/   
> using --RS-conf and also a new file in another directory. Nothing  
> changed.
>

Again, you wouldn't see that. Note that Rserve's default config file  
is located in /etc and *not* in $R_HOME/etc. You can override the  
default by defining CONFIG_FILE macro at compile time if you wish, but  
--RS-conf myRserve.conf is usually sufficient.


> Trying to establish a remote connection I get a RserveException:
> Handshake failed... .
>
> What did I wrong?
>

Hard to say - you didn't tell us exactly how you started Rserve. See  
the FAQ for telnet test on whether Rserve works (you get the ID  
lines), some firewall is blocking it (you cannot connect) or remote  
access is disabled (connection is established, but closed immediately).

Cheers,
Simon

The above is not a valid config file, but you know that, right? I'm  
not sure whether you're showing --RS-settings output or the config  
file, but make sure you don't confuse them...


> What's a little bit strange: the reported settings still did not   
> change. But as long as I get the connection...I don't care.
>
> Another question is the security. Now I enabled remote access,   
> authorization would be a good thing. How does this work? I created

It seems you didn't enable authentication. Please make sure your  
config file is valid (see the docs for its format) ... it should look  
somewhat like:
remote enable
pwdfile /foo/Rserve/users
auth required

Cheers,
Simon
